lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: Excuse me, is there a post office near here?
lines.spa: Disculpe, ¿hay una oficina de correos cerca de aquí?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: Yes, there is. Go straight on and turn left at the traffic lights.
lines.spa: Sí, la hay. Vaya derecho y doble a la izquierda en el semáforo.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: Is it far from here?
lines.spa: ¿Está lejos de aquí?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: No, it's about five minutes on foot. It's next to the bank.
lines.spa: No, está a unos cinco minutos a pie. Está al lado del banco.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: Thank you very much!
lines.spa: ¡Muchas gracias!

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: You're welcome. Have a nice day!
lines.spa: De nada. ¡Que tenga un buen día!

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: Where are you going, Leo?
lines.spa: ¿Adónde vas, Leo?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: I am going to the cinema to meet my cousins.
lines.spa: Voy al cine a encontrarme con mis primos.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: Do you know the way?
lines.spa: ¿Conoces el camino?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: Yes. Cross the bridge and turn right into High Street.
lines.spa: Sí. Cruza el puente y dobla a la derecha en High Street.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: The cinema is opposite the park, right?
lines.spa: El cine está enfrente del parque, ¿verdad?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: Exactly! See you later.
lines.spa: ¡Exacto! Nos vemos luego.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: Look at all this plastic on the grass!
lines.spa: ¡Mira todo este plástico en el pasto!

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: That's terrible. People shouldn't drop litter here.
lines.spa: Eso es terrible. La gente no debería tirar basura aquí.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: Let's take action. Put on these gloves and take a bag.
lines.spa: Tomemos acción. Ponte estos guantes y agarra una bolsa.

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: Good idea. I can collect the cans and plastic bottles.
lines.spa: Buena idea. Puedo juntar las latas y botellas plásticas.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: Then we can put them into the recycling bin.
lines.spa: Luego podemos ponerlas en el contenedor de reciclaje.

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: Our park will look beautiful again.
lines.spa: Nuestro parque volverá a verse hermoso.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: Shh! Don't shout in the library, please.
lines.spa: ¡Shh! No grites en la biblioteca, por favor.

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: Sorry! I forgot the rules.
lines.spa: ¡Perdón! Me olvidé de las reglas.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: Turn off your mobile phone or put it on silent.
lines.spa: Apaga tu teléfono celular o ponlo en silencio.

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: Can we eat our snacks in here?
lines.spa: ¿Podemos comer nuestros refrigerios aquí adentro?

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: No, don't eat or drink near the books.
lines.spa: No, no comas ni bebas cerca de los libros.

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: Understood. Let's finish our research quietly.
lines.spa: Entendido. Terminemos nuestra investigación en silencio.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: How do you usually travel to school?
lines.spa: ¿Cómo sueles viajar a la escuela?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: I ride my bicycle every morning.
lines.spa: Voy en bicicleta todas las mañanas.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: That produces zero air pollution!
lines.spa: ¡Eso produce cero contaminación del aire!

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: Yes, and it's great exercise too.
lines.spa: Sí, y además es un ejercicio genial.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: I want to ride my bike with you tomorrow.
lines.spa: Quiero ir en bici contigo mañana.

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: Great! Don't forget your helmet.
lines.spa: ¡Genial! No te olvides del casco.

READING_COMPREHENSION.readingText: Curitiba is a famous city in southern Brazil. Decades ago, the city decided to take action to protect the environment and make life better for its citizens. Instead of building expensive underground trains, they designed a fast bus system that millions of people use every day. Curitiba also has more than thirty public parks with lakes and trees. In poor neighbourhoods, the city started a special programme: residents collect rubbish from the streets and trade it for fresh fruits, vegetables, and bus tickets. Today, Curitiba is an inspiring example of a sustainable city.

READING_COMPREHENSION.readingText: To get to the City Museum from the central train station, exit through the main doors onto Station Road. Walk straight on for two hundred metres until you reach the clock tower. Turn right into King Street. Walk past the baker's and the chemist's. On your left, you will see a big park with a fountain. Cross the pedestrian crossing carefully. The museum is a grand stone building located directly opposite the fountain, between the library and the art gallery. Admission is free for school students.

READING_COMPREHENSION.readingText: Lucas and his sister Sofia noticed several stray cats and dogs near their neighbourhood park. Instead of ignoring the problem, they decided to take action. First, they spoke to a local animal rescue charity. Then, they organised a weekend car wash at their school to raise money. With the money they raised, they bought pet food, blankets, and medicine. Volunteers helped take the animals to the vet for vaccinations. Now, three puppies already have loving new homes. Lucas says: 'When young people work together, we can change our community.'
